_comment: SPARK — S157 LANDED STINK BAG atlas spec. Consumed DIRECTLY by scripts/build-sprite-atlas.mjs:
node scripts/build-sprite-atlas.mjs assets-source/stink-bag/atlas-spec.json
⚠ This is a FLAT spec, unlike godly-goblins/atlas-specs.json which wraps five of them in a
`specs` array — the builder reads `spec.states` off the top level, so that file has to be split
before it can be run and this one does not.
ONE STATE. A landed bag idles until it is destroyed; it does not walk and it has no attack
animation (the aura IS the attack, and an aura is a state readout the renderer paints, not art).
CLIP CHOICE — `clips/stink-bag-tight-a`, chosen against three rejected siblings. See
clip-spec.json for the full audition; the deciding measurements were:
· stink-bag-breathe : sack lost its speckles and its split healed shut. REJECTED (drift).
· stink-bag         : sack held, but the plume grew without bound and from frame ~40 the
content bbox top hits y=0 — the plume would ship sliced flat by the
cell edge. REJECTED (clipping, and no window returns to its start).
· stink-bag-tight-b : plume held, but its grey fuse smoke thickened until it competed with
the green, and its best loop cost was 14.5. REJECTED (worse loop, and
the green is the whole point of the object).
· stink-bag-tight-a : SHIPPED. bbox top stays 40..82 (never touches the frame edge) and its
best loop cost is 10.4 vs an 18.5 whole-clip baseline.
⭐ sampleStart 0 + sampleWindow 72 IS THE SEAMLESS LOOP, AND IT IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN.
The builder derives stride = floor(sampleWindow / framesPerState) = floor(72/12) = 6, so the
cells are source frames 0, 6, 12 ... 66 and the loop wraps 66 -> 0 across a 72-frame gap. Every
(start, stride) pair with stride in 2..8 was scored by mean absolute grey difference between
f[start] and f[start + 12*stride] — the pixels the wrap actually jumps between — and (0, 6) won
at 10.4 against 18.5 for the default whole-clip sampling. start=0 wins for a structural reason,
not a lucky one: frame 0 IS the seed image, and this clip's vapour returns toward its opening
shape at ~3 s. ⛔ Do not 'simplify' this by dropping the window back to the whole clip — that is
the setting that pops.
⭐ cellW/cellH 128 (vs 200 for a goblin, 240 for the tower). Deliberate: a landed bag is a small
ground prop, not a character. The union bbox measures 644x626 source px, so at height-fit the
sprite lands at 124x120 inside a 128 cell and cellW is never widened. 12 cells => a 1536x128
atlas, which is roughly a fortieth of the tower's sheet — and it lazy-loads from public/, so it
never enters the JS entry chunk that the bundle cap guards.
⭐ ticksPerFrame 15 = THE RATE IT WAS SHOT AT, derived rather than picked. Source is 24 fps and
the stride is 6, so consecutive cells are 6/24 = 0.25 s apart; at PHYSICS_HZ 60 that is 15 ticks
per frame and a 180-tick (3 s) loop. Every sibling is snappier (goblin idle 7, tower idle 6)
because they are creatures; a bag lying on the ground stinking should waft lazily, and playing
it at its native rate is also the only value that looks exactly like the clip that was
auditioned.
⭐ enclosedWhiteLimitPct 0.0001 (= 52px of 518400) is MEASURED on this art, not inherited. The
S152 goblins use 0.0002 because their enclosed background pockets ran 446..14291px. This prop
has none of those: its largest enclosed near-white component across frames 0/6/30/66 is 261px
(the interiors of the flies' dashed flight loops, which must go), while every real feature that
must stay opaque — the pale highlight dots on the burlap — is <= 23px. An 80..261 vs <=23 gap,
so 52 sits cleanly in the middle. NOTE the cream neck-cord and the fuse stub are NOT at risk:
they measure min-channel <= 205 and never register as near-white at all.
name: stink-bag
